source.title: Pattern separation in the dentate gyrus and CA3 of the hippocampus.

confidence_rationale: Canonical primary ephys (Moser lab, Science) showing the dentate gyrus decorrelates similar inputs before they reach CA3 -- direct mechanistic support for a separation stage upstream of the downstream associative network. Confidence held below 0.85 only by the transfer from spatial place-coding to REE's z_world planning seed.
failure_signatures: Pattern separation in this study is observed on the SPATIAL place-code; the experiment does not test that separating a planning SEED reduces near-duplicate trajectory proposals -- that downstream consequence is REE's extrapolation, not a measured result here.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Minimal changes in environment shape substantially alter correlated activity among dentate granule cells, while CA3 recruits non-overlapping assemblies -- a DUAL mechanism: decorrelation in DG plus recruitment in CA3.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-147's requirement that a DG-equivalent sparse layer decorrelate similar z_world seeds before the hippocampal module proposes rollouts. Crucially, the paper's dual mechanism also supplies the completion-set partner MECH-147 presupposes: CA3 recurrent recruitment (pattern COMPLETION) is the counterpart to DG separation, so a REE separation layer that omits a completion/recruitment stage would only implement half the circuit.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The paper measures decorrelation of a spatial code under environment-shape change; it does not show that this decorrelation improves trajectory-proposal diversity or planning. The REE consequence (separation -> non-duplicate rollouts) is a forward inference.
mapping.source_context: Single-unit recordings from place-modulated granule cells in freely-exploring Long-Evans rats under controlled environment-morph manipulations.

confidence_components.notes: High source quality (definitive primary result). Mapping fidelity strong for the separation stage; the rollout-diversity consequence is inferred. Transfer risk moderate (rodent spatial code -> REE latent planning seed).
